findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

csf.interpretation: Mildly elevated CSF protein, a non-specific finding. Cell count and glucose normal.

additional_observations: No mass, midline shift or hydrocephalus
ct.impression: Non-contrast CT head: no acute intracranial abnormality. Impression: normal non-contrast CT of the head.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings.description: 20 fiber pairs. Mean MCD 72 microseconds (reference <35). Increased jitter in 15 of 20 pairs (75%); blocking in 26% of pairs.

output.impression: Abnormal single-fiber EMG of the extensor digitorum: markedly increased jitter with impulse blocking, consistent with a disorder of neuromuscular transmission. Clinical correlation recommended.
FVC 3.30 L (88% predicted, 39 mL/kg), MEP 88 cmH2O and effective cough within reference limits; MIP -64 cmH2O at the lower limit of normal. No respiratory muscle weakness at present.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: AChR binding antibody 8.0 nmol/L with elevated blocking antibody; MuSK negative; CK and thyroid function normal
action_criteria.label: Order AChR binding antibody and thyroid function
action_criteria.rationale: Fatigable head drop with bulbar symptoms points to a disorder of neuromuscular transmission; AChR binding antibody is the first-line test and TSH screens for thyroid disease (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025; Evoli A et al., Neurol Sci 2019).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Decrement of 19% neck extensors, 16% trapezius, 12% nasalis, none in ADM; normal needle EMG
action_criteria.label: Order repetitive nerve stimulation including neck and facial muscles, with needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: In axial-predominant weakness RNS of proximal and facial muscles is more sensitive than distal limb RNS; needle EMG separates MG from neck extensor myopathy and motor neuron disease (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No anterior mediastinal mass; thymic involution appropriate for age
action_criteria.label: Order mediastinal CT with contrast to look for thymoma
action_criteria.rationale: Thymic imaging is indicated in every patient with MG; a thymoma would need resection at any age (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC 88% predicted (39 mL/kg), MIP -64 and MEP 88 cmH2O, effective cough
action_criteria.label: Measure baseline respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP)
action_criteria.rationale: Dysphagia and dysphonia are bulbar involvement and the planned steroids can cause early worsening: baseline FVC, MIP and MEP stage the respiratory risk (Lawn ND et al., Arch Neurol 2001).

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Markedly increased jitter with blocking in extensor digitorum
action_criteria.label: Single-fiber EMG (not needed when RNS is diagnostic)
action_criteria.rationale: RNS already shows a decrement in three muscles with positive AChR antibodies; single-fiber EMG adds no diagnostic information but is not wasteful.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No interaction with the current medicines; statin association noted
action_criteria.label: Check his medicines against pyridostigmine
action_criteria.rationale: Metformin, amlodipine, aspirin and atorvastatin have no pharmacokinetic interaction with pyridostigmine; optional.

action_criteria.label: Review guidance on the management of generalized myasthenia gravis
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading on management; not a clinical step in the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not start high-dose prednisone (above 20 mg/day) as an outpatient; start low and titrate, or start high dose only with inpatient monitoring, because initial steroid-induced worsening can precipitate crisis.

Avoid fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, macrolides and IV magnesium unless no alternative exists and the patient is monitored; use non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers only at reduced dose with quantitative monitoring.
Do not attribute the head drop to Parkinson disease antecollis and start or escalate dopaminergic treatment instead of treating MG.
required_recommendations: Diagnose AChR antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis with axial (neck extensor) predominance and mild bulbar weakness, MGFA class IIIa: fatigable head drop, AChR binding antibody 8.0 nmol/L, decrement in neck, trapezius and facial muscles with a normal needle EMG, no thymoma; the parkinsonism does not explain the head drop.
Start pyridostigmine 30 mg three times daily, titrating to effect up to 60 mg four to five times daily, watching for bradycardia given his coronary disease.

Start prednisone low (10-20 mg/day, increasing by 5-10 mg every 3-7 days) with bone protection and close glucose monitoring and diabetes treatment adjustment, and add an early steroid-sparing agent (azathioprine after TPMT testing) to limit steroid exposure [Sanders_2016].
Fit a soft or head-supporting cervical collar for the head drop while treatment takes effect.
Arrange speech and language therapy swallowing assessment with diet modification as needed, and advise him to seek care at once for choking, worsening dysphagia or breathlessness.

avoided_actions.rationale: EEG has no role in a disorder of the neuromuscular junction (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025).
CSF has no role in MG (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025); no CNS or Miller Fisher alternative is raised here.
FDG-PET is not indicated in MG; mediastinal CT covers thymoma screening (Jacob S et al., Pract Neurol 2025).
His coronary disease is stable and asymptomatic; echocardiography does not contribute to the diagnosis of MG.
No palpitations, syncope or arrhythmia; cardiac monitoring does not contribute to the diagnosis of MG.

accepted: AChR antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis with isolated neck extensor predominance (head drop)

differential.key_features: Isolated head drop in an older man raises it, but the weakness is fatigable, AChR antibodies are present, RNS shows a decrement and the needle EMG has no myopathic change.

Hypomimia, bradykinesia, rigidity, festination and reduced nigral SWI signal support coexisting parkinsonism, but antecollis comes from anterior neck rigidity, not 2/5 extensor weakness, and the decrement and AChR antibodies explain the head drop.
MRI shows spondylosis without cord compression or signal change; limb strength, reflexes and sensation are normal.
No wasting, fasciculations or upper motor neuron signs and a normal needle EMG without denervation.
Limbs are 5/5 with no finger flexor or quadriceps weakness, CK is normal and the needle EMG has no myopathic change.
Atorvastatin has been taken unchanged for years; CK is normal and the needle EMG shows no myopathy.

key_clinical_evidence: Four months of head drop with 2/5 neck extensor weakness, worse in the evening, plus mild fatigable dysphagia and dysphonia; limbs 5/5, no ptosis.
Coexisting parkinsonism (hypomimia, bradykinesia, asymmetric rigidity, festination) and a father with Parkinson disease.
AChR binding antibody 8.0 nmol/L with elevated blocking antibody; MuSK negative; CK and thyroid function normal.
RNS: decrement of 19% in neck extensors, 16% in trapezius and 12% in nasalis with none in ADM; normal needle EMG.

Mediastinal CT with contrast is indicated in every patient with MG to detect thymoma. Here it shows no thymoma; at 73 thymectomy is not routinely indicated without thymoma (MGTX enrolled patients up to 65).
Head drop is a recognized presentation of late-onset MG and must be separated from neck extensor myopathy, motor neuron disease and parkinsonian antecollis.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The nigral SWI change may accompany coexisting parkinsonism or age, but it does not explain fatigable neck extensor weakness, which the decrement and AChR antibodies attribute to MG.
red_herrings.data_point: Mildly reduced nigral signal on SWI
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute the head drop to Parkinson disease antecollis and miss MG.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Parkinson antecollis results from anterior neck rigidity, not true extensor weakness; 2/5 fatigable neck extensor weakness with a decrement is MG.
red_herrings.data_point: Parkinson-like features (hypomimia, bradykinesia, rigidity) suggesting antecollis from Parkinson's disease
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute the head drop to Parkinson disease antecollis, given the parkinsonian signs and the family history.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: There is no cord compression or signal change and the limb examination is normal; spondylosis is incidental.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute the head drop to cervical spondylotic myelopathy.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Atorvastatin is long-standing, CK is normal (78 U/L) and the needle EMG has no myopathic change; the RNS decrement and AChR antibody establish MG.
red_herrings.data_point: Atorvastatin as potential cause of myopathy
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute the neck weakness to statin myopathy.

sequence_constraints.reason: AChR antibody testing precedes single-fiber EMG; SFEMG is reserved for seronegative patients or a normal RNS (Jacob 2025).
Repetitive nerve stimulation is done first; SFEMG follows when RNS is normal (Jacob 2025).

findings.description:
CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST

Indication: Evaluation for thymoma

FINDINGS: No anterior mediastinal mass. Thymic involution appropriate for age. No lung mass. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. Lung bases clear.

IMPRESSION: No thymoma. Normal chest CT.

interactions: Metformin, amlodipine, aspirin: no clinically relevant interaction with pyridostigmine.
Atorvastatin: no pharmacokinetic interaction with pyridostigmine. Statins have been reported to unmask or worsen myasthenia gravis in case reports; causality is not established.
pyridostigmine.summary: No interactions between pyridostigmine and the current medicines; statins carry a reported, unproven association with worsening of myasthenia gravis.
warnings: Pyridostigmine: muscarinic adverse effects include increased secretions, diarrhea, cramps and bradycardia; use with care in coronary artery disease.

findings:
ELECTROCARDIOGRAM

RHYTHM: Sinus rhythm 70 bpm
PR 176 ms, QRS 92 ms, QTc 440 ms
Normal axis. Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy. No ischemic ST-T change. No arrhythmia.
ecg.interpretation: Sinus rhythm with voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy; no ischemic change or arrhythmia.

labs.interpretation: AChR binding antibody elevated (8.0 nmol/L) and AChR blocking antibody elevated (62%). MuSK antibody not detected. CK, TSH and free T4 within reference ranges. HbA1c 7.4%, consistent with known type 2 diabetes. AChR binding antibodies are found in most patients with acquired autoimmune myasthenia gravis; clinical correlation recommended.

myasthenia gravis.query: myasthenia gravis diagnosis and treatment guidance

results.finding: Consensus guidance recommends AChR antibody testing first, MuSK testing when AChR antibodies are absent, and electrodiagnostic confirmation by repetitive nerve stimulation or single-fiber EMG. Chest CT or MRI is recommended in all patients to detect thymoma.
results.source: Sanders DB et al., Neurology 2016;87:419-425; Narayanaswami P et al., Neurology 2021;96:114-122

results.finding: In the MGTX trial thymectomy improved outcomes over three years in non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.
results.source: Wolfe GI et al., N Engl J Med 2016;375:511-522 (MGTX)

myasthenia gravis.summary: Consensus guidance (Sanders 2016; update Narayanaswami 2021): AChR antibody testing first, MuSK when AChR antibodies are absent, RNS or single-fiber EMG for electrodiagnostic confirmation, chest CT or MRI in all patients for thymoma. MGTX (Wolfe 2016): thymectomy improved three-year outcomes in non-thymomatous AChR-positive generalized MG aged 18-65.

mri.impression: MRI brain and cervical spine: 1. Mild multilevel cervical spondylosis without cord contact, cord compression or cord signal change. 2. Mildly reduced signal of the substantia nigra on susceptibility-weighted imaging, of uncertain significance at this age. 3. No acute intracranial abnormality.

findings.description: 3 Hz trains of 10 stimuli; skin temperature 33 C; no anticholinesterase medication taken.
Baseline CMAP 3.1 mV; decrement 1st to 4th response 19%.
Baseline CMAP 9.0 mV; decrement 5%. After 10 s maximal contraction CMAP 9.2 mV; no facilitation.
Cervical paraspinal, deltoid, first dorsal interosseous, vastus lateralis and tibialis anterior: no fibrillation potentials or fasciculations; normal motor unit potentials and recruitment.

specialized_test.impression: 1. Decrement of 12-19% at 3 Hz in neck extensor, trapezius and nasalis muscles. 2. No decrement in abductor digiti minimi; normal baseline CMAP amplitudes; no post-exercise facilitation. 3. Normal needle EMG, with no neurogenic or myopathic change. Findings are consistent with a postsynaptic disorder of neuromuscular transmission with axial and cranial predominance. Clinical correlation recommended.

metadata.condition_name: Late-onset AChR+ MG presenting as head drop with coexisting parkinsonism
metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate: head drop in a man with parkinsonism invites antecollis, myelopathy or myopathy; AChR antibody and an axial RNS decrement with a normal needle EMG establish MG.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 3 required actions (AChR serology with thyroid function, RNS with neck and facial muscles, mediastinal CT), respiratory function recommended; 4 red herrings (nigral SWI change, parkinsonism, cervical spondylosis, atorvastatin); axial-predominant AChR+ MG.

patient.chief_complaint: Head drop, mild dysphagia and dysphonia, with parkinsonian features

family_history: Father had Parkinson's disease; no family history of autoimmune or neuromuscular disease
past_medical_history: Mild cervical spondylosis on prior imaging

social_history.note: Retired engineer; non-smoker; non-drinker; lives with wife; minimally active due to neck drop symptoms

patient.history_present_illness:
A 73-year-old man was admitted to the neurology ward with progressive neck extensor weakness and an inability to hold his head upright. Over about 4 months the head drop had worsened so that he needed to support his chin with his hand when seated or walking; it was mildest on waking and worst in the evening and after walking. Over the past 2 months he had also noticed mild dysphagia for solids and a hoarse, quieter voice, both worse at the end of meals and conversations. He denied ptosis, diplopia, limb weakness, breathlessness or sensory symptoms. His father had Parkinson disease. He did not smoke or drink alcohol. His regular medicines were metformin, amlodipine, aspirin and atorvastatin, the statin taken unchanged for six years.

His past medical history included type 2 diabetes mellitus, coronary artery disease (managed conservatively), arterial hypertension and mild cervical spondylosis on prior imaging. On neurological examination he was alert with hypomimia, mild bilateral bradykinesia and asymmetric limb rigidity (right more than left). There was no ptosis and extraocular movements were full. Neck extensor power was 2/5 bilaterally, with 5/5 strength in all four limbs, shoulder girdle and hip girdle muscles. Cognition was intact (MMSE 28/30). Gait was slightly shuffling with mild festination.

neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: No ptosis. Full extraocular movements without diplopia. Hypomimia. No facial weakness. Palate elevates symmetrically; tongue normal in bulk and strength.
neurological_exam.gait: Slightly shuffling gait with mild festination.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert; MMSE 28/30. No significant cognitive impairment. Hypomimia.
neurological_exam.motor: Neck extensors 2/5 bilaterally (cannot hold the head up against gravity); neck flexors 4/5. All limb muscle groups 5/5. No wasting or fasciculations. Mild bilateral bradykinesia. Asymmetric rigidity (right > left).

physical_exam.cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs
physical_exam.general: Alert; hypomimia; head drop, supporting his chin with his hand to keep the head upright. Weight 84 kg, height 174 cm.
physical_exam.neurological: Alert; MMSE 28/30. No ptosis. Full extraocular movements. Hypomimia. Mild bilateral bradykinesia. Asymmetric rigidity (right > left). Neck extensors 2/5 bilaterally, neck flexors 4/5; limbs 5/5. No fasciculations. DTR 2+ symmetric. Sensation intact. Slightly shuffling gait with mild festination.
physical_exam.respiratory: Chest clear to auscultation; no accessory muscle use; speaks in full sentences.
